what_happened: Dispatch rationale cited docs/book-convention.md and docs/architecture-decisions.md in the Verification repo (/home/benjamin/Projects/Logos/Verification) with specific mention counts; those files were relocated (books/convention.md; records/architecture-decisions.md split into per-decision files) since the dispatch text was written. File-count footprint (8 files match bare v[0-9] under docs/+README.md) still verified correct; per-file mention counts are stale. Plan should re-verify at implementation time rather than trust dispatch numbers.

Dispatch instructed adding the new standard to manifest.json's provides.context, modeled on the sibling. Verified provides.context is directory-name granularity (e.g. 'standards'), not file-level -- the sibling's own standards/task-reference-exemptions.md has no individual provides.context entry. The new context/standards/record-version-exemptions.md is already covered by the existing 'standards' entry; no provides.context edit is needed. Only provides.rules and provides.scripts need new filename entries.

Cross-checked the proposed blocking/advisory tiering against live content in the Verification repo: bare 'supersedes' and bare past-tense vocabulary (no longer/previously/formerly/used to) both occur pervasively in legitimate, accepted decision-record prose with zero version framing, confirming these must stay advisory/non-blocking unless co-occurring with a bare v[0-9] token. This gives the taxonomy a concrete, evidence-based escalation rule instead of a guessed word list.

Plan-time measurement found the eager-context budget at EXACTLY zero headroom: measure-eager-context.sh reports TOTAL 65950 B against orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes of 65950 B. Adding a new frontmatter-absent (eager) rule file plus a merge-sources/claudemd.md bullet will overshoot verify-deploy gate 20 sub-check B by roughly 1.8-2.1 KB. Discovered during planning rather than at the final gate, so the plan carries a dedicated budget-reconciliation phase using the trim-and-relocate precedent already recorded twice in that config's own note.

The research report's wiring correction (manifest.json provides.context is a directory-level array, so the new standards file needs no entry) was independently re-confirmed in one python3 read during planning, saving the implementer from adding a spurious non-conforming file-level manifest entry that the dispatch text literally instructed.
